args.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Greyline battlefield game animation bitmap sprite sheet.
Output: ONE 2048 x 2048 square PNG with genuine alpha transparency. Background pixels must be truly transparent, never painted white, black, gray, or checkerboard. Preserve soft partial alpha at wispy edges.
Layout: Exactly SIXTEEN independently drawn consecutive animation cels of ONE event, in a strict uniform 4-column x 4-row grid. Read left-to-right then top-to-bottom, frames 0 through 15. Each cell is one quarter of the canvas width and height (512 x 512 when the sheet is 2048 square). The grid is invisible: no borders, dividers, frame numbers, labels, captions, UI, watermarks or text.
Framing: Every cel contains the WHOLE effect at that moment. Fixed camera, fixed world scale, fixed origin throughout all 16 cells; expansion and dissipation change the effect, never the camera or cell scale. Keep every part of the largest effect, every detached debris fleck, and every soft alpha fringe inside the central 76% of its own cell, x=12%-88%, y=12%-88%. Leave the margins completely transparent. Large clear separation; adjacent images must never touch. No slices or strips from any neighboring frame; no cropped tips, debris, or smoke.
Style: Detailed painterly game cel animation with realistic muted military combat colors, tangible fine earth/smoke texture and crisp organic contours that remain readable at small game scale. Natural irregular forms and believable variation within one evolving event. Not 8-bit pixel primitives, flat vector cartoons, repeated stamps, blurry blobs, photographic background scenes, or fuel-explosion spectacle.
Continuity: A single chronological event, never a row of separate explosions and never a looping restart. Frames 0-2 are tiny initial-flash stages; frames 3-5 are the expanding peak; frames 6-9 dissipate into smoke/debris; frames 10-15 are faint, progressively more dissipated residue. NO renewed flash, new blast, or new dense cloud in any late frame. The last cel must still contain a faint visible remnant, not be empty.
Scene/backdrop: Isolated effect only on alpha; no scenery, ground surface, floor, horizon, objects, people, weapons, vehicles, lighting backdrop, cast-shadow plane or decorative elements.

Subject: ONE high-explosive ground blast. A low, broad ochre dust crown, with a very brief orange-white explosive core and irregular flying dark dirt clods. The silhouette is wide and squat with uneven outward-raking fingers of dirt and layered earth dust. This is a high-explosive soil impact, not a fuel fireball, not a tall earth pillar and not a mushroom cloud.
Origin: The ground contact/emission origin is fixed at x=50%, y=88% of EVERY cell. Dust spreads laterally and upward from that point; all visible material and fading fringes remain above or at y=88%, inside the safe box. Do not move the base between frames.
Palette: Muted ochre, khaki, umber, dusty warm gray, dark soil; restrained orange-white only during the brief early explosive flash. No sustained orange flames.
Frame progression, one cel per listed frame:
Row 1: 0 tiny pinpoint orange-white flash at the origin, a trace of dust; 1 tiny sharper flash with a few fresh dirt grains; 2 still-small initial flash with a low beginning ochre crown; 3 expanding low broad crown, short orange-white core and irregular dirt fingers.
Row 2: 4 broad near-peak ochre crown with core rapidly fading; 5 maximum broad dust-crown extent and separated dirt clods, core extinguished; 6 dust crown loosens into broken lobes and outward falling soil; 7 thinner broad dusty turbulence with falling clods.
Row 3: 8 dissipating uneven dust and fewer small clods; 9 flatter, lighter, fragmented dust veil; 10 faint broken ochre wisps, no flame; 11 even fainter separated dusty remnants, less visual mass than frame 10.
Row 4: 12 very faint low drifting dust; 13 sparser and more transparent small wisps; 14 barely visible irregular ochre residue; 15 the faintest still-visible low dust trace. Late frames progressively lose opacity and mass, never grow into a fresh blast.
Return only this one complete 16-cel sheet.

Subject: ONE fragmentation grenade ground blast, visibly distinct from a heavy HE shell blast or fuel fireball. A sharp, very short pale flash followed by compact asymmetric gray-brown dust and only a few dark flying fragments. The dust is small and irregular, with one side slightly more extended, never a large symmetric fireball or broad heavy ochre wall. Mostly dust by frame 5.
Origin: The ground contact/emission origin is fixed at x=50%, y=88% of EVERY cell. The effect expands upward and sideways from that point; all visible material and fading fringes remain above or at y=88%, inside the safe box. Do not shift the base between frames. Keep the grenade effect compact relative to the cell, including its few fragments.
Palette: Pale ivory flash, muted cool gray, gray-brown dust, dark charcoal fragments. Minimal warmth; no orange sustained fire or fuel glow.
Frame progression, one cel per listed frame:
Row 1: 0 tiny pale pinpoint flash at the origin; 1 tiny narrow sharp ivory flash with a few dust grains; 2 small brief jagged pale flash and a compact asymmetric puff beginning; 3 compact expanding irregular gray-brown dust with a narrow pale flash already fading and a few detached fragments.
Row 2: 4 compact peak expansion, irregular dusty lobes, barely any pale light; 5 mostly gray-brown dust with the flash effectively gone, only a few visible fragments; 6 broken compact dust lobes and dark fragments moving out; 7 thinner uneven dust, fragments beginning to fall.
Row 3: 8 lighter broken dust and only a couple of tiny dark fragment flecks; 9 sparse gray-brown residual dust; 10 faint separated dusty wisps; 11 less opaque and less substantial residue.
Row 4: 12 very faint small irregular dust traces; 13 even sparser almost-transparent remnants; 14 barely visible dusty residue; 15 a faint still-visible final dust trace. No late sparks or renewed flash. Each of the last six cels has progressively less opacity and visual mass.
Return only this one complete 16-cel sheet.

Subject: ONE airborne flak burst. A compact white-yellow star flash becomes irregular charcoal radial smoke lobes, then sparse dissipating dark fragments and faint smoke/dust residue. It floats in open alpha space and expands radially from its center. Never render a ground blast, ground plume, bottom base, downward supporting stem, pedestal, tall column, or mushroom cloud.
Origin: The explosion center is fixed at x=50%, y=50% of EVERY cell. Radial development around that same center, with organic asymmetry but no overall center drift. All smoke, star points and detached fragments stay inside the central 76% safe box. Use the same scale and center through all sixteen frames.
Palette: Brief white-yellow early flash, neutral charcoal and muted dark gray lobes, dusty gray fading wisps and dark fragments. No long-lasting orange fireball or fuel flames.
Frame progression, one cel per listed frame:
Row 1: 0 tiny white-yellow star pinpoint at exact center; 1 slightly expanded but still tiny sharp star flash; 2 small compact multi-point flash with the first dark smoke knots; 3 expanding compact radial charcoal lobes with short pale rays rapidly dying.
Row 2: 4 near-peak irregular radial smoke lobes with only a trace of central pale light; 5 peak charcoal radial cloud, no bright core, a few detached dark flecks; 6 lobes separating with transparent gaps opening radially; 7 thinner separated charcoal lobes and a few outward fragments.
Row 3: 8 smoke becoming broken lighter gray wisps with dark debris flecks; 9 mostly sparse dark fragments and faint smoke around the original center; 10 faint smoke/dust residue and few tiny dark flecks; 11 progressively less opaque, fewer flecks, no light.
Row 4: 12 very sparse fading gray residue with a couple of tiny dim fragments; 13 still thinner partial-alpha residual wisps; 14 barely visible irregular gray traces near the same center; 15 a faint still-visible final dark-gray wispy remnant. Frames 10-15 monotonically lose opacity and visual mass, no flash or new smoke formation.
Return only this one complete 16-cel sheet.
